clue.text: At sea, I'll float fleet

indicators.note: being at sea is being confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor boasting that they will float out to sea with the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats sailing together.

clue.text: About five kilometres for the union

definitions.meaning: an old measure of distance, about three miles
an alliance or association of teams or nations

explanation.surface: A trade union march of roughly five kilometres.
explanation.definitionFit: The old distance measure of about three miles shares its spelling with an alliance of clubs or states.

clue.text: Small amount, nearly all, everything

parts.note: a tot is a small measure, especially of spirits

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A list of quantities: a little, almost the lot, the whole lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The total is the whole sum, everything counted together.

clue.text: Thief left fire-raiser, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word that follows is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: an arsonist deliberately sets fires

explanation.surface: A thief who has abandoned a fire-starter, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so one who commits it is a thief.

clue.text: Complicated trade with company offering particular style

indicators.note: complicated suggests something tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complicated business deal between firms that offer a distinctive style.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s with bold geometric forms.

clue.text: Walk short way then go on horseback

parts.note: ST is the short form of street, a way
to ride is to go on horseback

explanation.surface: Someone walks a little way and then mounts a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, so to stride is to walk purposefully.

clue.text: The last thing maths lecturer might do

definitions.text: The last thing maths lecturer might do

parts.words: The last thing maths lecturer might do
parts.note: a lecturer ends by summarising, and a mathematician adds numbers; the phrase covers both at the close of a lesson

explanation.surface: Something a maths lecturer would never dream of doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing' seems to mean something the lecturer would never do; it really means the final act of a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude a talk by summarising, while also suggesting adding numbers together.

clue.text: Talent cur misused, not being willing

indicators.note: misused means put to the wrong use, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gifted dog wasted, and refusing to cooperate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant is unwilling or hesitant to do something.

clue.text: Shop without obligation?

definitions.meaning: an airport store selling goods without import tax
a duty is an obligation, so free of it means exempt from one

explanation.surface: A shop where you can browse without being pressured to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport shops sell tax-exempt goods, and literally the phrase means free of any duty or obligation.

clue.text: Influence loud performer

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an actor is a stage performer

explanation.surface: A noisy performer exerting influence over others.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is something that has an influence on an outcome, a contributing element.

clue.text: Short-term worker not on time to produce pattern

parts.note: a temp is a temporary employee
late means not on time

explanation.surface: A temp turning up late at the office, yet somehow producing a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or model used as a guide for making copies.

clue.text: Sucker's target?

parts.note: the centre of a dartboard is a target, and a ... is also a striped boiled sweet, something to suck, so the sucker has its own target

explanation.surface: A con artist's mark: the gullible person targeted.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull's-eye is a traditional British hard peppermint sweet as well as the centre of a target; 'Sucker' hints at the sweet, not a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull's-eye is the centre spot of a target, and also a sweet sucked slowly.

clue.text: Calm down quickly if captured

indicators.note: the word for quick has taken prisoner the little word that follows it

parts.note: pacy means fast, moving quickly

explanation.surface: Telling someone to settle down fast if they have been caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or calm an agitated person or situation.

clue.text: Supports two old railway experts

parts.note: two of something is a pair of them
BR is British Rail, the former national railway
aces are experts or top performers

explanation.surface: Two retired railway specialists propping something up.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the UK's nationalised railway until the 1990s. Braces are what Americans call suspenders, straps holding trousers up.
explanation.definitionFit: Braces hold up trousers, so a set of them acts as supports.

clue.text: Power over living club official

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
a resident is someone living in a place

explanation.surface: Strength taking control over the living, as some club bigwig might.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the chief officer of a club or society.

clue.text: One might guard female captured by flier

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the bird that follows

parts.note: a bee-eater is a colourful bird, something that flies

explanation.surface: A guard dog keeps watch over a woman seized by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are ceremonial guards at the Tower of London.

clue.text: Short protest about sailor turning politician

parts.note: demo is short for demonstration, a protest
C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the word for sailor is written backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A brief protest about a sailor who turns into a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, a political figure.

clue.text: Powerful man having his way in London?

definitions.text: Powerful man having his way in London?

parts.words: Powerful man having his way in London?
parts.note: a ruler standing in for a monarch gives his title to a famous road in the capital, his own way

explanation.surface: A mighty man getting what he wants in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent Street is a major London shopping street named after the Prince Regent, later George IV; 'having his way' means owning a road, not getting what he wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in a monarch's place, and this famous London thoroughfare bears that title.

clue.text: Stout upended over cheese is silky stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece on top of the second
upended means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word for stout reads upwards

parts.note: stout means fat
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A tipped-over pint of stout spilled on some cheese, making something silky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer but means FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous fabric, often of silk.

clue.text: Meal to take out

parts.note: suggests a takeaway, but this is food packed up and taken outdoors to eat

explanation.surface: Ordering a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take out' suggests a takeaway, but this meal is carried out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal of packed food eaten in the open air.

clue.text: Tongue that's used to make things shiny

definitions.meaning: a tongue is a language, here the language of Poland

definitions.text: that's used to make things shiny
definitions.meaning: a wax or cream rubbed on furniture or shoes to bring up a gleam

explanation.surface: Licking something to make it gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the language spoken in Poland and a substance for making surfaces shine.

clue.text: Lady the lender houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A woman whose landlord provides her housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen is a woman's name, so a lady.

clue.text: Type of fiend that's found outside

definitions.meaning: a fiend here is an enthusiast; someone devoted to open-air walks is called a ... fiend
the clean open-air atmosphere is found outdoors

explanation.surface: A monster lurking outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes the idiom for an outdoors enthusiast and is also the clean atmosphere outdoors.

clue.text: Brother's ring seen underneath instrument

indicators.note: in a down entry the circle shape is placed below the instrument

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A brother's ring spotted under a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers, the American comedy team, famous for playing the harp.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo Marx was one of the comedic Marx Brothers.

clue.text: Genuine sportsman staunchly faithful

parts.note: true means genuine or real
a blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge university at sport

explanation.surface: An honest athlete who stays loyal through thick and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue is a British term for an Oxford or Cambridge athlete awarded colours for playing against the rival university.
explanation.definitionFit: True-blue describes someone utterly loyal, especially to a cause or political party.

clue.text: We backed abandoning the wrong crowd

indicators.note: leaving behind letters, so they are taken out of the phrase that follows
backed means turned round, so the two letters of We are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: We retreated, leaving the wrong crowd behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns WE into EW, and 'abandoning' removes those letters, E then W, from THEWRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large, densely packed crowd of people.

clue.text: New York perhaps withholding drug — trendy drug

indicators.note: holding back a letter, so it is left out of the word

parts.note: New York is an example of a US state
E is short for ecstasy, a drug
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A city refusing to supply one drug, while another drug is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Statins are cholesterol-lowering medicines, a class of prescription drug.

clue.text: Kind of blue? One follows in leader's plane

definitions.meaning: a particular greyish-blue shade is named after the uniforms of military aviators
add One after the words and you get the name of the US president's aircraft

explanation.surface: A sad mood, and someone tagging along on a chief's flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Air Force One is the call sign of the US president's aircraft, so 'One' follows the answer to name the leader's plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Air force blue is a named colour, and the military service lends its name to the president's jet.
